study: Holding period aligned with forecast horizon; second specification after replication.json
status: posthoc specification: proposed after the daily-rebalanced results of replication.json were seen; same 2016-2021 research sample, so it is not independent confirmation
inputs: predictions.parquet from replication.json, unchanged; no retraining, no new features, no parameter search

construction.daily_book: same as replication.json: median split, weights proportional to |percentile - mean|, each leg gross 1
construction.cohorts: overlapping Jegadeesh-Titman cohorts: the book formed at close t is held for H trading days; the held weight on day t is the sum of the last H daily books divided by H
construction.start: cohorts that would have been formed before the first prediction date are cash, so exposure ramps up over the first H days
construction.ensemble: equal-weight average of the eight horizon-aligned held books

variants.cohort: primary: cohort average as above, gross exposure at most 2
variants.renormalized: secondary: each day the positive part of the cohort average is scaled to gross 1 and the negative part to gross 1

execution.main: held weights from close t earn close t to close t+1

turnover: sum |w_t - w_{t-1}| of held weights plus 2|w| on each held symbol's dominant-contract roll day
comparators: daily-rebalanced results of replication.json (performance.csv), including the CARRY10 daily baseline, reported unchanged
hypotheses: H5: for 66d-200d, horizon-aligned holding has higher net Sharpe than daily rebalancing of the same predictions
H6: the horizon-aligned ensemble has higher net Sharpe than the daily-rebalanced ensemble (0.73)
H7: daily turnover of each horizon-aligned book falls roughly in proportion to 1/H
reporting: report every horizon, the ensemble, both variants, both timings, gross and net, including null and adverse results; count this as an additional specification when judging significance
